title: Git worktree manager
goal: Create, track, inspect and clean up git worktrees so each agent in branch mode works on its own branch without touching the user's main checkout.
scope_in: `WorktreeManager.create` running `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <baseRef>` by argv (no shell) under a configurable root (`worktree.root`, default `<repo>/.centcom/worktrees/`, auto-added to `.git/info/exclude`), branch name `centcom/<owner-slug>/<agent-slug>` validated with `git check-ref-format --branch`; collision handling appends `-2`, `-3` up to 20.

Registry `.centcom/worktrees.json` (atomic writes) mapping `agt_` id to path, branch, base ref, created_at; reconciled at startup with `git worktree list --porcelain` (orphans flagged, missing dirs pruned via `git worktree prune`).

`status(wt)` returning `{ branch, head, ahead, behind, dirty }` (same fields as the `branch.update` secret payload) using `git rev-parse`, `git rev-list --left-right --count base...HEAD`, `git status --porcelain=v1 -z`; ahead/behind are relative to the base ref recorded at creation.

`remove(wt, { force })` refusing to delete a dirty worktree or one with unmerged commits unless `force`; `list()`; `prune()`; `detectConflict(wt, otherRef)` using `git merge-tree --write-tree` (no working-tree changes) returning conflicted file list (relative paths) or empty.
Git hygiene: every call sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `LC_ALL=C`, timeouts (read 10 s, add/remove 30 s, merge-tree 30 s), stdout cap 4 MiB, argv arrays only.

Emits `worktree:created` / `worktree:removed` on the bus (C025); also exposes a helper `branchUpdatePayload(wt)` producing the secret `branch.update` body (`agent_id, branch, head, ahead, behind, dirty`).
scope_out: Merging branches, pushing, PR creation: later git lanes or the user.
File locks: lane C018. Sub-agent isolation policy: lane C024.
build_against: Real `git` against throwaway repos built by `tools/dev/make-fixture-repo.mjs` (lane C011) or by an in-test helper that runs `git init` in a temp dir with fixed identity; no network; git >= 2.38 required (merge-tree --write-tree).
interfaces: `createWorktreeManager(deps: { git: GitRunner; fs: WtFs; bus: AgentBus; ids: IdGenerator; clock: Clock; config: { root?: string } }): WorktreeManager`

`interface WorktreeManager { create(o: { repoRoot: string; agentId: AgentId; ownerSlug: string; baseRef?: string; label?: string }): Promise<Worktree>; list(repoRoot: string): Promise<Worktree[]>; status(w: Worktree): Promise<WorktreeStatus>; remove(w: Worktree, o?: { force?: boolean }): Promise<void>; prune(repoRoot: string): Promise<number>; detectConflict(w: Worktree, otherRef: string): Promise<string[]> }`

`interface Worktree { agentId: AgentId; path: string; branch: string; baseRef: string; repoRoot: string }`; `interface GitRunner { run(argv: string[], o: { cwd: string; timeoutMs: number; maxBytes: number }): Promise<{ code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string }> }`.
acceptance: `create` on a fixture repo yields a directory under `<repo>/.centcom/worktrees/`, a new branch `centcom/...`, and `git worktree list` shows it; the main checkout's `git status` stays clean and `.git/info/exclude` contains the root exactly once.
Branch name collisions: creating 3 worktrees with the same label produces `...`, `...-2`, `...-3`; a label with spaces, `..`, `~` or unicode is slugged to `[a-z0-9-]` and passes `check-ref-format`.
`status` after editing one file and committing another reports `dirty:true`, `ahead:1`, `behind:0`; after the base ref advances by 2 commits `behind:2`.
`remove` on a dirty worktree throws `DirtyWorktree`; with `{force:true}` removes directory, registry entry and branch reference worktree metadata; `list` no longer contains it.
Startup reconcile: deleting a worktree directory by hand then `list` marks it `missing` and `prune` removes the git metadata; an orphan registry entry is dropped.
`detectConflict` returns the exact conflicted relative paths for a two-branch edit of the same line and `[]` for non-overlapping edits, leaving both working trees untouched.
Every git call used argv arrays: a test with a repo path containing spaces, `$()` and `;` succeeds and executes nothing extra.
A hung git (fake runner never resolves) is rejected with `GitTimeout` after exactly the configured timeout (fake clock).
tests: hostile-paths.test.ts, timeout.test.ts, windows-paths.test.ts (path normalisation unit cases).
guardrails: MUST invoke git via `execFile`-style argv only; MUST NOT build shell strings or pass user text as an option (use `--` before refs/paths; refs validated first).
MUST NOT touch the main working tree, run `git clean`, `reset --hard`, `checkout -f` or force-delete branches except through `remove({force:true})` for worktrees this manager created.
MUST confine worktree paths under the configured root; reject roots that resolve (realpath) outside the repo parent or onto a system directory.
MUST NOT log branch names, paths or file names (they are secret fields on the wire); logs carry agent ids, counts and durations.
Registry writes MUST be atomic; MUST never delete a directory not recorded in the registry.
failure_modes: Repo is bare or git too old -> `GitTooOld`/`NotAGitRepo` with an actionable local message; agents can still run in the plain cwd (branch mode disabled).
Disk full mid-create -> rollback: remove partial directory and branch, registry unchanged.
Lock file `.git/index.lock` present -> retry 3 times with 200 ms jittered backoff then fail with `GitTimeout`-class error.
notes: Worktree root default is a product choice; `.centcom/` must stay out of the user's tracked files (hence `info/exclude`, not .gitignore). Requires git >= 2.38 for `merge-tree --write-tree`.
